subject: Energy
title: Texas 2021: Winter Storm Uri
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Texas 2021: Winter Storm Uri.

hook.text: In February 2021, a polar vortex froze Texas—knocking out gas, coal, wind, and nuclear plants simultaneously.

buildup.text: Natural gas pipelines froze, cutting fuel to gas plants—which provide the majority of Texas electricity.

discovery.text: Wind turbines froze (some lacked cold-weather packages), and demand for heating surged to record levels.

twist.text: Texas's isolated grid (ERCOT) couldn't import power from neighboring states—it had no meaningful interconnections.

climax.text: Millions lost heat and water for days—at least 246 people died. Wholesale prices hit $9,000/MWh, 300 times normal.

punchline.text: An isolated grid, a frozen state—winter exposed every weakness.

quiz.question: Why couldn't Texas import power during the 2021 freeze?
